Categories: EDA, PDF Solutions

Key takeaways ▼
By Niles Moser
The forces that could begin turning a decade of infrastructure investment into accelerating growth
1. Historical Context
In Has the Puck Finally Arrived?, I argued that PDF Solutions has spent more than a decade assembling the infrastructure required for an increasingly connected, data-intensive and ultimately agentic semiconductor manufacturing industry.
This essay asks the natural follow-up: If the puck has finally arrived, what happens next?
For the past six years, including the current calendar year, PDF Solutions has compounded revenue at approximately 20% annually. It has accomplished this while deriving the vast majority of its revenue from bleeding-edge logic, with less than 5% of semiconductor manufacturing data analyzed with conventional tools (according to the Exensio Aurora press release), before modern semiconductor architectures such as GAA, backside power delivery, HBM and advanced 2.5D/3D packaging began moving into mainstream production, and before AI agents across the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain were contemplated.
Those historical constraints are important because they are now beginning to change. And several of those changes could become meaningful growth catalysts for different parts of PDF Solutions.
2. Unlocking the Data Already Being Generated
Direct beneficiaries: Exensio / Aurora, secureWISE and Sapience Manufacturing Hub
One of the largest potential growth opportunities for PDF Solutions does not require semiconductor manufacturing to generate a single additional byte of data. The opportunity begins with making more use of the manufacturing data the industry already generates.
PDF Solutions stated in the Exensio Aurora announcement that in its experience, “less than 5% of semiconductor manufacturing data is analyzed with conventional tools.”
Exensio Aurora was purpose-built to change this constraint. Its architecture is designed to handle semiconductor manufacturing data at petabyte scale, addressing datasets that PDF Solutions describes as both extremely long and extremely wide.
As more manufacturing data is analyzed, more data will need to move through secureWISE’s pipes, while Sapience Manufacturing Hub should benefit from the increased collection and contextualization of that data.
Opportunity: Move from an environment in which less than 5% of semiconductor manufacturing data is analyzed toward one in which virtually all of the data already being generated can ultimately be analyzed.
3. Moving Beyond the Historical Advanced-Logic Revenue Base
Direct beneficiaries: Exensio / Aurora, eProbe / DirectScan, secureWISE, DEX and Sapience Manufacturing Hub
For most of its history, PDF Solutions’ revenue base has been heavily concentrated in leading-edge logic. That addressable market is now broadening.
As John Kibarian stated on the Q2 2026 earnings call:
“All participants in the semiconductor supply chain will need to leverage AI agents to be more nimble, innovative, and cost-effective.”
If that proves correct, the need for AI-driven manufacturing analytics, connectivity and data infrastructure will extend beyond leading-edge logic and memory IDMs to manufacturers of power semiconductors, analog and mixed-signal devices, RF/RFIC devices, MEMS and sensors, and other specialty semiconductors, as well as equipment OEMs, OSATs and other participants across the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain.
That broadening should benefit PDF Solutions across its platform: Exensio / Aurora through analytics; secureWISE and DEX through data movement; Sapience Manufacturing Hub through manufacturing-data collection and contextualization; and eProbe / DirectScan through electrical inspection across a wider range of semiconductor technologies.
Opportunity: PDF Solutions can expand from a historically concentrated advanced-logic revenue base into the full breadth of the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain. This is not simply customer diversification. It is TAM expansion.
4. “Explosion” in Semiconductor Manufacturing Supply Chain Data and Complexity
Direct beneficiaries: Exensio / Aurora, eProbe / DirectScan, secureWISE, DEX and Sapience Manufacturing Hub
As semiconductor architectures and packaging become more complex, the amount of manufacturing data generated will increase. PDF Solutions describes the combination of 3D architecture, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration as producing an “explosion of data.”
The major technology transitions include 3nm, 2nm and eventually angstrom-class leading-edge logic; the transition from FinFET to gate-all-around (GAA) transistor architectures; backside power delivery; increasingly complex HBM stacks; chiplets; 2.5D/3D integration and advanced packaging; and the expanding inspection, metrology and test requirements associated with manufacturing these devices.
The GAA and backside-power transitions are converging at the most advanced nodes, adding new manufacturing and integration challenges on top of conventional node scaling. At the same time, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration are dissolving the traditional boundary between front-end and back-end manufacturing and dispersing production more globally. PDF Solutions describes the resulting data as “growing more dimensional, more hierarchical, more geographically distributed, and increasingly ‘virtual.’”
Exensio Aurora was architected specifically for this expansion. Its data size is designed to be limited only by the analytics cluster, with performance designed to scale linearly as data volumes grow in width or length.
More complexity means more inspection and measurement, more data generated, more data moving across the manufacturing supply chain, and more data available for analysis. Each of these trends directly increases demand for different parts of the PDF Solutions platform.
Opportunity: PDF Solutions should benefit from the explosion in data created by increasing complexity across the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain.
5. AI Agents Across the Semiconductor Manufacturing Supply Chain
Direct beneficiaries: Exensio / Aurora, secureWISE, DEX and Sapience Manufacturing Hub
John Kibarian has characterized the industry as being in the “very early stages of AI transformation of semiconductor manufacturing and engineering” and said that “all participants in the semiconductor supply chain will need to leverage AI agents to be more nimble, innovative, and cost-effective.”
Historically, analytics usage has been bounded by human governance and human workflows. AI agents remove much of that constraint because they can access and analyze data 24/7 through agent-to-agent interactions across enterprises. The result should be a significant increase in the frequency with which semiconductor manufacturing data is accessed, transmitted and analyzed.
Opportunity: Agent adoption will almost certainly drive a major increase in both data traffic and analytics usage.
Conclusion
Over the coming quarters and years, the ability to analyze much of the 95% of semiconductor manufacturing data that has effectively been dark, the expansion of PDF Solutions’ addressable market beyond advanced logic, the explosion in data created by increasing complexity across the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain, and the emergence of 24/7 agentic workflows should combine to drive a meaningful acceleration in revenue growth.
The timing of these catalysts can be affected by semiconductor cycles, customer spending decisions and the pace of technology adoption. But cycles do not reverse technology roadmaps. Chip architectures will continue to become more complex. Advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration will continue to proliferate. The amount of data generated, collected, and analyzed will continue to expand. And as AI agents demonstrate meaningful ROI through improved yield, shorter time-to-market and greater manufacturing efficiency, their adoption across the semiconductor supply chain should become more important even if the semiconductor cycle turns.
The timing may be cyclical. The direction is structural.
